Meaning / Logic: #Consigners who completed signup process(signup success bottomsheet)
SQL:
SELECT signup_month, COUNT(DISTINCT consigner_user_code)
FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source
WHERE cx_segment = 'New'
  AND login_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 60
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic: Of signups whose 1st trip happened within specified n-conversion days
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(day, login_date, acq_date) <= 29
                           THEN consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM (SELECT consigner_user_code, login_date,
             MAX(CASE WHEN trip_rank = 1 THEN latest_acq_time END)
                 OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code)::date AS acq_date
      FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source WHERE cx_segment = 'New')
WHERE login_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 30;

Meaning / Logic: Share of signups who opened a vehicle-type browsing session within specified n-conversion days
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(day, f.login_date, v.vt_time) <= 29
                           THEN f.consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT f.consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source f
LEFT JOIN (SELECT consigner_code,
                  MIN(TIMESTAMP 'epoch' + created / 1000000.0 * INTERVAL '1 second') AS vt_time
           FROM fact_cx_vt_browsing GROUP BY 1) v
       ON v.consigner_code = f.consigner_user_code
WHERE f.cx_segment = 'New' AND f.login_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 30;

Meaning / Logic: Share of signups who raised any demand within specified n-conversion days
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(day, login_date, demand_date) <= 29
                           THEN consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source
WHERE cx_segment = 'New' AND login_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 30;

Meaning / Logic: Share of signups who got a confirmed DR within specified n-conversion days

Meaning / Logic: Of acquired Cxs matured 30 days, the share who took a 2nd trip within specified n-conversion days of the first.
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.demand_date < a.demand_date + 30
                           THEN a.consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT a.consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source a
LEFT JOIN fact_consigner_demands_lead_source b
       ON b.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code
      AND b.demand_time > a.demand_time
      AND b.trip_flag = 1 AND b.placement_rank = 2
WHERE a.cx_segment = 'New' AND a.trip_flag = 1
  AND a.demand_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 30;

Meaning / Logic: Same as above, but reaching the 4th trip.
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.demand_date < a.demand_date + 30
                           THEN a.consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT a.consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source a
LEFT JOIN fact_consigner_demands_lead_source b
       ON b.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code
      AND b.demand_time > a.demand_time
      AND b.trip_flag = 1 AND b.placement_rank = 4
WHERE a.cx_segment = 'New' AND a.trip_flag = 1
  AND a.demand_date <= CURRENT_DATE - 30;

Meaning / Logic:
Cxs with a first trip, who took ≥1 trip within 90 days of that acquisition date are retention base. 
Share of the qualified cohort that took a trip in a later 90-day bucket.
SQL:
WITH acq AS (
    SELECT consigner_user_code,
           MIN(CASE WHEN trip_rank = 1 THEN latest_acq_time END)::date AS acq_date
    FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source GROUP BY 1
),
qualified AS (
    SELECT a.consigner_user_code, a.acq_date
    FROM acq a
    JOIN fact_consigner_demands_lead_source f
      ON f.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code AND f.trip_flag = 1
     AND f.demand_date >= a.acq_date AND f.demand_date < a.acq_date + 90
    WHERE a.acq_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.active = 1 THEN x.consigner_user_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.consigner_user_code), 0)
FROM (SELECT q.consigner_user_code, q.acq_date,
             MAX(CASE WHEN f.trip_flag = 1
                       AND f.demand_date >= q.acq_date + 181
                       AND f.demand_date <  q.acq_date + 271 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active
      FROM qualified q
      JOIN fact_consigner_demands_lead_source f
        ON f.consigner_user_code = q.consigner_user_code
      GROUP BY 1, 2) x
WHERE CURRENT_DATE >= x.acq_date + 271

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: # Fulfilled placements
Demands that got converted into trips.
When counting trips use trip_end_time in group by.
% of accepted placements that converted into trips
SQL:
select demand_date, count(distinct case when accepted is not null and auto_cancelled is null and trip_flag = 1 then demand_id end)*1.0/nullif(count(distinct case when accepted is not null and auto_cancelled is null then demand_id end),0) as "% Acceptance to Trip"
from (
        select a.*
                        , fc.accepted
                        , cx.auto_cancelled
                        , cx.demand_id as cancelled 
                        from mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_demands_lead_source a 
                        left join (
                                select demand_id, max(gtl_time) as accepted
                                from mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full
                                group by demand_id
                        ) fc on a.demand_id = fc.demand_id
                        
                        left join (
                                select demand_id, max(case when cancel_remarks = 'AUTO_CANCELLED_NO_ACTIVITY' then cancel_time end) as auto_cancelled
                                from mp_analytics_core.fact_consignment_cancellations
                                group by demand_id
                        ) cx on a.demand_id = cx.demand_id
                        
                        where plc_flag=1 
)
group by 1

Meaning / Logic: % DR cancelled by consigner before placement
SQL:
WITH ss AS (
  select * 
        from(
                select 
                a.demand_id,
                a.sub_status,
                a.created_by,
                case when a.sub_status like 'DR%' then a.created end as dr_status_time,
                max(dr_status_time) over (partition by a.demand_id) as max_dr_status_time,
                lag(a.created) over (partition by a.demand_id order by a.created) as prev_created_time
                from mp_analytics_core.fact_demand_sub_status a
                where a.created >= '2025-10-01'
                ) a
        where prev_created_time = max_dr_status_time
)
select case when {{timeframe_type}} like 'DoD' then demand_date
                when {{timeframe_type}} like 'WoW' then demand_week
                when {{timeframe_type}} like 'MoM' then demand_month end as "Day/Week/Month"
        , count(distinct case when plc_flag = 0 and reason='CX_cancelled' then demand_id end)*1.0/nullif(count(distinct case when dr_flag = 1 then demand_id end),0) as "% DR(Cx Cancel)"

    from (
        select a.*
                , case when (b0.sub_status='CANCELLED' and b0.created_by!='consigner@wheelseye.com') or b0.sub_status in ('FREIGHT_PFC') then 'Vehicle_Not_Found' 
                              when b0.sub_status='CANCELLED' and b0.created_by='consigner@wheelseye.com' then 'CX_cancelled' end as reason   
        from mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_demands_lead_source
                left join base0 b0 on a.demand_id=b0.demand_id 
        )       
    group by 1

Metric: CX Initiated, CX Induced GTL cancellation
Meaning / Logic: % of accepted placements that got cancelled by Consigner and induced party was Consigner

select demand_date, 
,count(distinct case when cx_initiated_cx_induced=1 then demand_id end)*1.0/nullif(count(distinct case when accepted=1 then demand_id end),0) as "% cx_initiated_cx_induced"
from (
                select a.*, acc.accepted
                , case when acc.accepted = 1 and cxl.cx_cx = 1 then 1 else 0 end as cx_initiated_cx_induced
                , case when acc.accepted = 1 and cxl.cx_fo = 1 then 1 else 0 end as cx_initiated_fo_induced
                , case when acc.accepted = 1 and cxl.fo_fo = 1 then 1 else 0 end as fo_initiated_fo_induced

                        group by demand_id

                        , max(case when cancelled_by in ('consigner@wheelseye.com','SYSTEM') and induced_party = 'Operator'  then 1 else 0 end) as cx_fo

Metric: Vehicle replacement post GTL Cancellation(Reason : CX Initiated,CX Induced)
Meaning / Logic: % of post GTL cancellation that got re-placed (Cancellation by Consigner and induced party = Consigner)
SQL:
with cx_cancel as (
    select demand_id, min(cancel_time) as cx_cancel_time
    from mp_analytics_core.fact_consignment_cancellations
    where cancelled_by in ('consigner@wheelseye.com','SYSTEM')
      and induced_party = 'Consigner'
    group by 1
),
acc as (
    select demand_id, max(case when gtl_time is not null then 1 else 0 end) as accepted
    from mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full
    group by 1
),
repl as (
    select c.demand_id,
           max(case when f.consignment_time > c.cx_cancel_time then 1 else 0 end) as replaced
    from cx_cancel c
    join mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full f on f.demand_id = c.demand_id
    group by 1
),
fo as (
    select c.demand_id,
           1 as backout,
           case when r.replaced = 1 then 1 else 0 end as conv
    from cx_cancel c
    join acc a on a.demand_id = c.demand_id and a.accepted = 1
    left join repl r on r.demand_id = c.demand_id
)
select
case when {{timeframe_type}} like 'DoD' then demand_date
	 when {{timeframe_type}} like 'WoW' then demand_week
	 when {{timeframe_type}} like 'MoM' then demand_month end as "Day/Week/Month"
, count(distinct case when conv = 1 then demand_id end)*1.0
  / nullif(count(distinct case when backout = 1 then demand_id end),0) as "% cx_init_cx_ind_replaced"
from (select *
	from (
		select a.*, fo.conv, fo.backout
		from mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_demands_lead_source a
		join fo on a.demand_id = fo.demand_id
		)a
					)
group by 1,2

Meaning / Logic: Of placements the FO accepted and that were not auto-cancelled, the share that became a fulfilled trip.
SQL:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN accepted IS NOT NULL AND auto_cancelled IS NULL
                            AND trip_flag = 1 THEN demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN accepted IS NOT NULL AND auto_cancelled IS NULL
                                  THEN demand_id END), 0)
FROM (SELECT a.demand_id, a.demand_date, a.trip_flag, fc.accepted, cx.auto_cancelled
      FROM fact_consigner_demands_lead_source a
      LEFT JOIN (SELECT demand_id, MAX(gtl_time) AS accepted
                 FROM mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full GROUP BY 1) fc
             ON fc.demand_id = a.demand_id
      LEFT JOIN (SELECT demand_id,
                        MAX(CASE WHEN cancel_remarks = 'AUTO_CANCELLED_NO_ACTIVITY'
                                 THEN cancel_time END) AS auto_cancelled
                 FROM fact_consignment_cancellations GROUP BY 1) cx
             ON cx.demand_id = a.demand_id
      WHERE a.plc_flag = 1);

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: % Ready FO; % Ready Not Active in last 90 days

Share of cumulative Ready FOs who have NOT placed any token in the last 90 days — the dormant-Ready pool.
SQL:
WITH ready AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT operator_code
  FROM fact_operators_mp_events
  WHERE ready_fo = 1
),
recent_plc AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT operator_code
  FROM fact_operators_mp_events
  WHERE total_placed_loads > 0
    AND event_date >= CURRENT_DATE - 90

SELECT
  (COUNT(DISTINCT r.operator_code) - COUNT(DISTINCT p.operator_code)) * 1.0
  / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT v.operator_code), 0) AS pct_dormant_ready
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT operator_code FROM fact_operators_mp_events WHERE landed_on_mp = 1) v
LEFT JOIN ready r ON v.operator_code = r.operator_code
LEFT JOIN recent_plc p ON v.operator_code = p.operator_code;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: % Churn; Lapsed FOs.

Of Trip FOs in the cohort month, count and % whose LAST trip date is more than 1 month before today — i.e., have stopped tripping.
SQL:
WITH cohort AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT operator_code, DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date) AS cohort_month
  FROM fact_operators_mp_events
  WHERE total_trips_loads > 0
),
last_trip AS (
  SELECT operator_code, MAX(event_date) AS last_trip_date
  FROM fact_operators_mp_events
  WHERE total_trips_loads > 0
  GROUP BY operator_code
)
SELECT
  c.cohort_month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.last_trip_date < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month'
                      THEN c.operator_code END) * 1.0
  / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT c.operator_code), 0) AS churn_pct
FROM cohort c JOIN last_trip l USING (operator_code)
GROUP BY c.cohort_month;

Meaning / Logic:

Lifecycle cohort tag assigned to each FO based on number of completed trips. Values:

  • "1-2"  → Early Retention (1-2 trips)
  • "2+"   → Retained FOs (more than 2 trips — fully retained)

Used as a split / cohort filter, NOT as a standalone metric. Pair with any FO-Growth count or %
(e.g., # Trip FO by fo_segment) to see how the funnel performs per lifecycle stage.
SQL:
SELECT DISTINCT fo_segment
FROM fact_operators_mp_events;
-- (table sometimes referred to as fact_fo_mp_events)

SELECT
  fo_segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT operator_code) AS fo_count
FROM fact_operators_mp_events
WHERE landed_on_mp = 1
GROUP BY fo_segment;

on a.demand_id=b.demand_id

left join

from consignments_data ) c

Metric: DR with minimum time for Matching
Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: DR with minimum time for BA, DR with minimum time for Booking Automation

DR which were active minimum x minutes to find vehicle. Standard is 30 minutes is not specified.
SQL:
select count(a.demand_id)
from mp_analytics_core.fact_demands a
left join mp_analytics_core.dim_consigners b on a.consigner_user_code=b.consigner_user_code
where a.load_type='FTL' and b.customer_type ilike '%%sme%%' and b.customer_flag='WE_Customer' and a.status='FULFILLED'
and (case when a.plc_flag=0 then datediff('minutes', a.dr_time, coalesce(a.demand_cancel_by_cx_time, a.demand_cancel_by_sys_time)) else 10000 end) >= 30

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: 2A. Avg Opsearch FOs Per DR; Supply Quantity Appearing in DRs.

Average number of distinct operators surfaced by Opsearch against a confirmed DR. Measures how deep the matchable supply pool is per demand. Split by Demand Region (NCR / ROI / Others) or Overall; weekly grain.
SQL:
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('week', f.demand_date)::date              AS week_start,
    f.demand_region                                      AS split,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN f.demand_id END) AS total_drs,

    -- Avg Opsearch FOs per DR
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN o.total_operators::float END), 1) AS avg_opsearch_fos_per_dr,


FROM mp_analytics_core.mp_demand_details f
LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_core.fact_demand_opsearch_summary o
       ON o.demandid = f.demand_id
WHERE f.metadata_plt != 'true'
  AND f.customer_type != 'ENTERPRISE'
  AND f.customer_flag  = 'WE_Customer'
  AND (f.consigner_freight_fare > 1000 OR f.consigner_freight_fare IS NULL)
  AND f.demand_date >= DATEADD(week, -12, DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE))
  AND f.demand_date <  DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

Metric: Avg Trip FO Ratio per DR
Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: 2B. Avg Trip FO Ratio Per DR; Quality of Supply in DR.

Of the operators surfaced in Opsearch for a DR, the share that are already trip-experienced (had their 1st trip before the demand date). Ratio = Avg Trip-Opsearch FOs per DR / Avg Opsearch FOs per DR. Tells whether the matched pool is real supply or dormant supply.
SQL:
SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('week', f.demand_date)::date              AS week_start,
    f.demand_region                                      AS split,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN f.demand_id END) AS total_drs,


    -- Avg Trip FOs per DR
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN o.trip_fo::float END), 1)         AS avg_trip_fos_per_dr,

    -- Trip FO Ratio
    AVG(CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN o.trip_fo::float END)
      / NULLIF(AVG(CASE WHEN f.dr_flag = 1 THEN o.total_operators::float END), 0) AS trip_fo_ratio

FROM mp_analytics_core.mp_demand_details f
LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_core.fact_demand_opsearch_summary o
       ON o.demandid = f.demand_id
WHERE f.metadata_plt != 'true'
  AND f.customer_type != 'ENTERPRISE'
  AND f.customer_flag  = 'WE_Customer'
  AND (f.consigner_freight_fare > 1000 OR f.consigner_freight_fare IS NULL)
  AND f.demand_date >= DATEADD(week, -12, DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE))
  AND f.demand_date <  DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: 3A. Supply Quality Funnel - New Token FO's; First-Time Token Payers.

Operators who paid a token in the period AND had never paid one before (token_till_date - is_token_paid_loads = 0). Distinct from '# Token Paid FO', which counts all token payers including repeats.
SQL:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', e.event_date)::date AS week_start,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.is_token_paid > 0
                            AND (e.token_till_date - e.is_token_paid_loads) = 0
                           THEN e.operator_code END) AS new_token_fos
FROM analytics.fact_operators_mp_events e
WHERE e.landed_on_mp = 1 AND e.fo_sub_type = 'Subs'
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: 4C. Newly Activated FOs; New Trip FOs; First-Trip Activations.

Operators who took a trip in the period AND had zero trips before it (trips_till_date - total_trips_loads = 0). This is the supply-side activation counter on the Supply Quality Funnel; '# Acquired FOs' is the equivalent on the FO Growth dashboard.
SQL:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', e.event_date)::date AS week_start,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.total_trips_loads > 0
                            AND (e.trips_till_date - e.total_trips_loads) = 0
                           THEN e.operator_code END) AS newly_activated_fos
FROM analytics.fact_operators_mp_events e
WHERE e.fo_sub_type = 'Subs'
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: visitor_to_va_pct; Visitor → Vehicle Available %.

Of operators who landed on MP in the week, the share who marked a vehicle AVAILABLE in the availability snapshot. Step 2 of the Supply Quality Funnel (Visitors → VA → LDP → Token → Trip). Note: VA numerator comes from a separate snapshot table, so region splits must join on week+region.
SQL:
WITH veh_avail AS (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', avs.snapshot_time)::date AS week_start,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN avs.remark='AVAILABLE' THEN avs.op_code END) AS avail_fos
  FROM analytics.apollo_vehicle_availability_snapshot avs
  JOIN analytics.fact_operators_onb onb ON avs.op_code = onb.operator_code AND onb.sub_date > '1970-01-01'
  JOIN analytics.fact_operators_mp_events fp ON fp.operator_code = avs.op_code AND fp.landed_on_mp = 1
  GROUP BY 1)
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', e.event_date)::date AS week_start,
       100.0 * va.avail_fos / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT e.operator_code),0) AS visitor_to_va_pct
FROM analytics.fact_operators_mp_events e
LEFT JOIN veh_avail va ON va.week_start = DATE_TRUNC('week', e.event_date)::date
WHERE e.landed_on_mp = 1 AND e.fo_sub_type = 'Subs'
GROUP BY 1, va.avail_fos;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: First to 2nd Trip Activation (In 7/14/30/60/90 Days); FO Trip Cohort.

Cohort of FOs by the week of their FIRST trip; share who took a 2nd (or 3rd) trip within n days of it. n = 7 / 14 / 30 / 60 / 90 for 2nd trip, 7 / 14 / 21 for 3rd. Available Pan-India and split by FO Region (NCR / ROI / OTHERS). More granular version of '% Acquired to 2nd Trip'.
SQL:
WITH raw_ AS (
  SELECT c.operator_code, c.consignment_time::date AS placement_date,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.operator_code ORDER BY c.consignment_time) AS ranker
  FROM mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full c
  WHERE c.consignment_state != 'CANCELLED'
    AND c.demand_id IN (SELECT demand_id FROM mp_analytics_core.mp_demand_details
                        WHERE metadata_plt != 'true' AND customer_type != 'ENTERPRISE'
                          AND customer_flag = 'WE_Customer'
                          AND (consigner_freight_fare > 1000 OR consigner_freight_fare IS NULL))
), cohort AS (
  SELECT operator_code,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ranker=1 THEN placement_date END) AS first_trip_date,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ranker=2 THEN placement_date END) AS second_trip_date
  FROM raw_ GROUP BY 1)
SELECT date_trunc('week', first_trip_date)::date AS week,
       COUNT(DISTINCT operator_code) AS first_trip_fos,
       100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN second_trip_date <= first_trip_date + 30 THEN operator_code END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT operator_code),0) AS pct_2nd_trip_30d
FROM cohort GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Consignment Pickup - Ontime %; Reached at Loading Ontime.

Share of completed trips where the vehicle reached the loading point on time (gtl_delay = 'ontime'). Denominator = trips completed in the period (by unloading_done_time). FTL only.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', s.unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.gtl_delay = 'ontime' THEN s.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.demand_id), 0) AS pickup_ontime_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats s
WHERE s.business_type = 'FTL' AND s.unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Consignment Delivery - Ontime %; In TAT - Delivery.

Share of completed trips that reached unloading within the system transit TAT. CAUTION: two different flag values are in use across cards — sys_trnst_dly = 'in_tat' on the Pickup card and sys_trnst_dly = 'ontime' on the NPS/Critical-Delays cards. Confirm which the consuming card uses before comparing numbers.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', s.unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.sys_trnst_dly = 'in_tat' THEN s.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.demand_id), 0) AS delivery_ontime_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats s
WHERE s.unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Transit Critical Delays %; Over 20% TAT Trips.

Share of completed trips where transit overshot the system TAT by more than 20% (sys_trnst_dly = 'over_20%_TAT'). Feeds the 'Churn - Critical Cases' watchlist along with damage trips.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', s.unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.sys_trnst_dly = 'over_20%_TAT' THEN s.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.demand_id), 0) AS critical_delays_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats s
WHERE s.unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Damage Trips %; Damage Occurred in Trips %; YoY Damage Trips %.

Share of completed trips with any damage/shortage recorded, i.e. damage type NOT IN ('nan','NO_DAMAGE','None',''). Split available NCR vs ROI and New vs Onboarded.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', s.unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.type NOT IN ('nan','NO_DAMAGE','None','') THEN s.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.demand_id), 0) AS damage_trips_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats s
WHERE s.unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Trip NPS; NPS.

Net Promoter Score on post-trip ratings. Promoters = rating 5; Passives = rating 4; Detractors = rating 1-3. NPS = %Promoters − %Detractors, both taken over RATED trips only (rating > 0), not all trips. Split by NCR vs ROI, New vs Onboarded, HP vs LP.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating = 5 THEN demand_id END) * 1.0
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating > 0 THEN demand_id END), 0)
     - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating IN (1,2,3) THEN demand_id END) * 1.0
         / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating > 0 THEN demand_id END), 0) AS nps
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats
WHERE unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Bad Rated Trips %.

CAUTION — two definitions coexist on the dashboard. NPS-family cards use rating IN (1,2,3); the Pickup/Service-Overview card uses rating IN (1,2). Denominator in both is ALL completed trips, not rated trips. Always state which cut is being quoted.
SQL:
-- NPS-family definition (rating 1-3):
SELECT date_trunc('month', unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating IN (1,2,3) THEN demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT demand_id), 0) AS bad_rated_trips_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats
WHERE unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

-- Service-Overview definition swaps the numerator to: rating IN (1,2)

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Total Trips V/s Rating Received Trips; Rated_Trips%.

Share of completed trips that received any rating (rating > 0). This is the coverage denominator for NPS and Average Trip Rating — a low value means NPS is being read off a thin, self-selected sample.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rating > 0 THEN demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT demand_id), 0) AS rated_trips_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats
WHERE unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Tickets Per Trip; CX - Tickets WOW/MOM; Tickets per Trip - App / Manual Split.

Consigner tickets raised per completed trip. Tickets from mp_analytics_core.fact_cx_tickets (by ticket_created_time), trips from fact_consigner_service_stats (by unloading_done_time). Split by source APP vs ODIN, and available excluding 'PAYMENT MAPPING' sub-issues.
SQL:
WITH trips AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', unloading_done_time) AS timeline, COUNT(DISTINCT code) AS trips
  FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats
  WHERE unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1),
tickets AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', ticket_created_time) AS timeline,
         COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_code) AS tickets,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source = 'APP'  THEN ticket_code END) AS app_tickets,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source = 'ODIN' THEN ticket_code END) AS odin_tickets
  FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_cx_tickets GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.timeline,
       k.tickets * 1.0 / NULLIF(t.trips, 0) AS tickets_per_trip,
       k.app_tickets  * 1.0 / NULLIF(k.tickets, 0) AS app_tickets_pct,
       k.odin_tickets * 1.0 / NULLIF(k.tickets, 0) AS odin_tickets_pct
FROM trips t LEFT JOIN tickets k ON k.timeline = t.timeline;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: escalation_raised_in_trips%.

Share of completed trips on which the consigner raised at least one ticket. Trip-level (unlike Tickets per Trip, which is ticket-level and can exceed 1).
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', s.unloading_done_time) AS trip_completion_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tk.ticket_code IS NOT NULL THEN s.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.demand_id), 0) AS escalation_raised_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_consigner_service_stats s
LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_core.fact_cx_tickets tk ON tk.demand_id = s.demand_id
WHERE s.unloading_done_time IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Escalation Solved Ontime %; In TAT Resolution % - App & Manual Tickets.

Share of consigner tickets resolved within their issue-wise TAT (tat_resolve_cat = 1). Also reported split by source (APP vs ODIN).
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', ticket_created_time) AS ticket_created_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tat_resolve_cat = 1 THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_code), 0) AS in_tat_resolution_pct,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tat_resolve_cat = 1 AND source = 'APP' THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source = 'APP' THEN ticket_code END), 0) AS app_in_tat_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_cx_tickets
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: App Tickets CSAT; good_feeback_on_app_tkts%.

Of app-raised consigner tickets that received feedback, the share marked GOOD. Feedback coverage is reported alongside as feebacks_on_app_tkts% = (GOOD + BAD) / app tickets. Overall CSAT uses the same formula without the source = 'APP' filter.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', ticket_created_time) AS ticket_created_time,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source='APP' AND ticket_feedback='GOOD' THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source='APP' AND ticket_feedback IN ('GOOD','BAD') THEN ticket_code END), 0)
         AS good_feedback_on_app_tkts_pct,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source='APP' AND ticket_feedback IN ('GOOD','BAD') THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN source='APP' THEN ticket_code END), 0) AS feedback_coverage_pct
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_cx_tickets
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Operator Backout %; Post-Acceptance-Fo-ind%.

Of ACCEPTED placements, the share cancelled after acceptance with induced_party = 'Operator'. Attribution overrides: cancelled_by containing 'SYSTEM', or cancel_remarks containing 'RETRY_BETTER_PRICE', are re-attributed to Consigner. Also reported pre-acceptance (FO / Cx induced) and as a demand-loss cut.
SQL:
WITH cons AS (
  SELECT fc.demand_id, fc.consignment_code, fc.consignment_time, fc.gtl_time AS acceptance,
         CASE WHEN strpos(upper(COALESCE(fcc.cancelled_by,'')),'SYSTEM') > 0 THEN 'Consigner'
              WHEN strpos(upper(COALESCE(fcc.cancel_remarks,'')),'RETRY_BETTER_PRICE') > 0 THEN 'Consigner'
              ELSE fcc.induced_party END AS induced_party,
         fcc.cancel_time
  FROM mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full fc
  LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_core.fact_consignment_cancellations fcc ON fcc.consignment_code = fc.consignment_code),
scope AS (SELECT demand_id, status FROM mp_analytics_core.mp_demand_details
          WHERE metadata_plt != 'true' AND customer_type != 'ENTERPRISE' AND customer_flag = 'WE_Customer'
            AND (consigner_freight_fare > 1000 OR consigner_freight_fare IS NULL))
SELECT date_trunc('week', DATE(c.consignment_time)) AS timeline,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.acceptance IS NOT NULL AND c.cancel_time > c.acceptance
                            AND c.induced_party = 'Operator' THEN c.demand_id END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.acceptance IS NOT NULL THEN c.demand_id END), 0) AS post_acceptance_fo_ind_pct
FROM cons c JOIN scope s ON s.demand_id = c.demand_id
GROUP BY 1;

Metric: Balance Payment TAT (post valid POD upload)
Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Balance Payment On Basis Of Valid POD Upload.

Same bucketing as Balance Payment TAT but the clock starts at the POD collection entry time (or trip end, whichever is later) instead of trip end. Use this when the question is 'how fast do we pay once the FO has done their part'; use the trip-end version for the FO's lived experience.
SQL:
-- Identical to Balance Payment TAT (post Trip End), except the reference time is:
--   finl_time = GREATEST(unloading_done_time, pod_collection_entry_time)
-- bal_time_diff = DATEDIFF(minute, finl_time, bal_pay_time)
-- Buckets: <=120 / <=360 / <=720 / <=1440 / >1440 minutes over the same 'balance_paid' denominator.

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Operator Advance Payment; LessThan1Hr/2Hr/6Hr/12Hr/24Hr %.

Of trips where an advance was paid, the share disbursed within 1 / 2 / 6 / 12 / 24 hrs of trip start. Trip start = otp_entry_time, falling back to in_transit_time when OTP is missing. Advance = latest SUCCESS DEBIT txn of type 'ADVANCE'. Optional NCR flag filter.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', unloading_done_time)::date AS month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT code) AS total_trips,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN time_dispose IS NOT NULL THEN code END) AS advance_paid,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN adv_time_diff <= 60   THEN code END)*100.0/NULLIF(advance_paid,0),2) AS lt1hr_pct,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN adv_time_diff <= 360  THEN code END)*100.0/NULLIF(advance_paid,0),2) AS lt6hr_pct,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN adv_time_diff <= 1440 THEN code END)*100.0/NULLIF(advance_paid,0),2) AS lt24hr_pct
FROM (
  -- trip_start_time = COALESCE(otp_entry_time, in_transit_time)
  -- adv_time_diff  = DATEDIFF(minute, trip_start_time, adv_pay_time)
  SELECT ... FROM mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full c
  LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_ops.fact_operator_consignment_transaction x
         ON split_part(c.consignment_code,'-',2) = x.consignment_id
        AND x.type='ADVANCE' AND x.status='SUCCESS' AND x.category='DEBIT'
  WHERE c.consignment_state = 'TRIP_END')
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Tickets Per Trip Fulfilled Trips; Tickets Per Trip Placed Trips; Operator Tickets Per Trip.

Operator tickets raised per trip. Two denominators are in use — Fulfilled trips and Placed trips — and they are NOT interchangeable; the placed-trip version is always lower. Tickets from mp_analytics_core.fact_operator_tickets (a_created); trips from fact_consignments where consignment_state != 'CANCELLED', with the standard non-PTL / non-Enterprise / WE_Customer / fare>1000 scope.
SQL:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('day', t.a_created::timestamp) AS date_trip,
         COUNT(DISTINCT t.ticket_code) AS tickets
  FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_operator_tickets t GROUP BY 1),
trips AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('day', c.consignment_time) AS date_trip,
         COUNT(DISTINCT c.consignment_code) AS trips_done
  FROM mp_analytics_critical.fact_consignments_full c
  LEFT JOIN mp_analytics_core.mp_demand_details d ON d.demand_id = c.demand_id
  WHERE c.consignment_state != 'CANCELLED'
    AND metadata_plt != 'true' AND customer_type != 'ENTERPRISE' AND customer_flag = 'WE_Customer'
    AND (consigner_freight_fare > 1000 OR consigner_freight_fare IS NULL)
  GROUP BY 1)
SELECT date_trunc('month', trips.date_trip) AS month,
       SUM(tickets) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(trips_done), 0) AS tickets_per_trip
FROM trips LEFT JOIN a ON a.date_trip = trips.date_trip
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: IN TAT Resolution %; IN_TAT_%.

Share of operator tickets resolved within an issue-wise TAT measured in HOURS. TAT lookup is per issue_identified (e.g. Operator Backout 1h, No Response from Customer 2h, most charge/detention issues 3h, Delay in POD 6h, Advance/Balance Payment 12h, Delay in Loading/Unloading 24h, UTR issues 72h, Damage/Shortage 168h). Duration = resolved_dur for RESOLVED/CLOSED, open_from for ACTIVE/HOLD. Note: open_from carries a known IST-offset quirk, preserved from the legacy query.
SQL:
WITH tat_calc AS (
  SELECT t.ticket_code, t.a_created::timestamp AS a_created, t.issue_identified, t.status,
         CASE WHEN t.status IN ('RESOLVED','CLOSED') THEN t.resolved_dur
              WHEN t.status IN ('ACTIVE','HOLD')     THEN t.open_from END AS resolved_duration,
         CASE WHEN t.issue_identified = 'Operator Backout' THEN 1
              WHEN t.issue_identified = 'No Response from Customer' THEN 2
              WHEN t.issue_identified IN ('Delay in Bilti','Loading Charge','Unloading Charge',
                   'Loading Detention','Unloading Detention','Extra Distance') THEN 3
              WHEN t.issue_identified = 'Delay in POD' THEN 6
              WHEN t.issue_identified IN ('Advance Payment','Balance Payment') THEN 12
              WHEN t.issue_identified IN ('Delay in Loading','Delay in Unloading') THEN 24
              WHEN t.issue_identified IN ('Advance UTR Not Generated','Balance UTR Not Generated') THEN 72
              WHEN t.issue_identified = 'Damage / Shortage Issue' THEN 168
              /* ...full lookup in card 31305... */ END AS tat
  FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_operator_tickets t WHERE t.a_created::timestamp >= '2024-04-01')
SELECT date_trunc('month', a_created) AS month_,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN resolved_duration <= tat THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_code), 0) AS in_tat_pct
FROM tat_calc GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Overall FO Queries; tickets_per_trip / calls_per_trip / chats_per_trip / rm_calls_per_trip.

Single scorecard putting every FO contact channel on one per-trip denominator: tickets (fact_operator_tickets), CC calls (cc_acd_raw), chats (tesseract_help_chat_session), and RM calls (mp_rm_call_details_raw, CONNECTED only, split MP_Load_Support_Inbound vs _Outbound). Use it to see channel substitution — chat deflection should push tickets_per_trip down, not just chats_per_trip up.
SQL:
-- trips: fact_consignments (state != 'CANCELLED', non-PTL, non-Enterprise, WE_Customer, fare>1000)
-- tickets: COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_code) FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_operator_tickets
-- calls:   COUNT(DISTINCT call_id) FROM cc_acd_raw JOIN cc_crm_raw (product='Marketplace', c_type='Customer')
-- chats:   COUNT(DISTINCT sessionid) FROM mp_analytics_sandbox.tesseract_help_chat_session
-- rm:      COUNT(DISTINCT call_id) FROM analytics.mp_rm_call_details_raw WHERE system_disposition='CONNECTED'
SELECT month,
       total_tickets * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_trips,0) AS tickets_per_trip,
       total_calls   * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_trips,0) AS calls_per_trip,
       total_chats   * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_trips,0) AS chats_per_trip,
       rm_total_calls * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_trips,0) AS rm_calls_per_trip
FROM base_agg LEFT JOIN rm_calls_agg USING (month);

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Operator App (Chat Auto Redressal); chats_converted_to_ticket%.

Of operator help-chat sessions, the share that ended up creating a ticket (ticket created at or after chat start). This is the inverse of auto-redressal: lower = the bot resolved it. Sessions where the linked ticket predates the chat are classified 'ticket_created_before_chat' and excluded from the numerator.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', chat_created) AS chat_created,
       COUNT(DISTINCT sessionid) AS unique_chat_sessions,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ticket_chat_chck = 'ticket_created_in_chat' THEN sessionid END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT sessionid), 0) AS chats_converted_to_ticket_pct
FROM (
  SELECT cs.sessionid, cs.created_ts + interval '5h30m' AS chat_created,
         CASE WHEN datediff(min, cs.created_ts + interval '5h30m', tms.ticket_creation) >= 0
              THEN 'ticket_created_in_chat'
              WHEN datediff(min, cs.created_ts + interval '5h30m', tms.ticket_creation) < 0
              THEN 'ticket_created_before_chat' END AS ticket_chat_chck
  FROM mp_analytics_sandbox.tesseract_help_chat_session cs
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ticket_code, created + interval '5h30m' AS ticket_creation
             FROM trucking.dpdtms_ticket) tms ON tms.ticket_code = cs.ticketid)
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Chats CSAT; Overall Chat CSAT; chats_recieved_good_feebacks%.

Of operator chat sessions that received feedback, the share with feedbackcategory = 'SATISFIED'. IMPORTANT: tesseract_help_chat_feedback is CDC-replicated with multiple rows per sessionid — dedup to the latest row per session (ROW_NUMBER over updated desc, id desc) before aggregating, or sessions double-count into both good and bad buckets.
SQL:
WITH cf AS (
  SELECT sessionid, feedbackcategory FROM (
    SELECT sessionid, feedbackcategory,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY sessionid ORDER BY updated DESC, id DESC) AS rn
    FROM mp_analytics_sandbox.tesseract_help_chat_feedback WHERE deleted = false)
  WHERE rn = 1)
SELECT date_trunc('month', cs.created_ts + interval '5h30m') AS chat_created,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cf.feedbackcategory = 'SATISFIED' THEN cs.sessionid END) * 1.0
     / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cf.feedbackcategory IS NOT NULL THEN cs.sessionid END), 0)
         AS chat_csat
FROM mp_analytics_sandbox.tesseract_help_chat_session cs
LEFT JOIN cf ON cf.sessionid = cs.sessionid
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Overall FO Ticket Feedbacks : MP; %feedback / %feedback_- / %feedback_+.

Three things on one card: (1) feedback coverage = tickets with feedback / total tickets; (2) negative rate = NOT_SATISFIED / tickets with feedback; (3) dissatisfaction reason mix over total tickets — DELAY_IN_RESOLUTION, INAPPROPRIATE_RESOLUTION, NO_UPDATES, TEAM_MISCONDUCT, OTHERS. Reason % denominators are TOTAL tickets, not feedback-received, so they will not sum to the negative rate.
SQL:
SELECT date_trunc('month', a_created::date) AS ticket_creation,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_code) AS total_tickets,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN len(ticket_feedback) > 3 THEN ticket_code END) AS feedback_received,
       feedback_received * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_tickets, 0) AS "%feedback",
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ticket_feedback = 'NOT_SATISFIED' THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
         / NULLIF(feedback_received, 0) AS "%feedback_-",
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ticket_feedback_reason ILIKE '%DELAY_IN_RESOLUTION%' THEN ticket_code END) * 1.0
         / NULLIF(total_tickets, 0) AS "delay_in_resolution%"
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_operator_tickets
GROUP BY 1;

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: # Requirements; # Consignor Requirements.

Count of distinct PTL shipment *requirements* (not raw rate-API calls). Replaces the older "price checks" count.

Grain fix: fact_ptl_browsing is at RATE-API-CALL grain — a new browsing_id is minted on every re-quote, which overstates demand ~4x. This metric collapses calls into requirements:
1. BURST = a consignor's chain of rate calls; a gap of >=30 min starts a new burst (runs across midnight, no calendar-day cut).
2. REQUIREMENT = one lane (pickup_pincode + drop_pincode) inside one burst. Two lanes in a burst = 2 requirements; same lane on another day = 2 requirements.
3. QUALIFYING — APP: needs >=1 deviation from the app's hardcoded prefill (drop pincode / weight / dimensions). WEB PORTAL: always qualifies (requirement is stated to a KAM, not inferred).
4. REPRESENTATIVE ROW = within a requirement, the latest row carrying dimensions; else simply the latest. Ground truth overrides the heuristic — a booked row is always its own requirement, so 100% of booked browsing_ids carry is_requirement = 1.

Service type is deliberately EXCLUDED from the deviation score (app ships WAREHOUSE_TO_WAREHOUSE default while 82% of bookings are DOOR_TO_DOOR — it predicts nothing).

Validation (1,351 Aug-2026 bookings): representative-row rule recovers the booked weight in 95.1% of booked requirements. Aug 1-26 baseline: 50,573 rate calls -> 12,787 requirements (~4.0x correction).
Caveat: 4.0% of demands carry NO browsing_id at all and are structurally unlinkable to a price check — if this share grows, the metric understates demand. Requirement -> Demand is NOT 1:1.

Definition locked 27 Aug 2026. Owner: PTL Demand POD.
Filters: Interval (Day/Week/Month), cx_segment_ptl, exp_type, consigner_region.
SQL:
/* =============================================================================
   PTL CONSIGNOR REQUIREMENT — STANDING METRIC
   =============================================================================
   Owner        : PTL Demand POD
   Purpose      : Replace "price checks" (raw rows in fact_ptl_browsing) with
                  "requirements" — one row per distinct shipment intent.
   Last updated : 27 Aug 2026

   WHY THIS EXISTS
   ---------------
   fact_ptl_browsing is at RATE-API-CALL grain, not user-action grain. A new
   browsing_id is minted on every rate call, including the silent re-quotes
   
   fired when a consignor edits anything while sitting on the transporter
   listing page. Counting rows overstates consignor demand ~4x.

   DEFINITION (locked 27 Aug 2026)
   -------------------------------
   1. BURST      A consignor's chain of rate calls; a gap of >= 30 minutes
                 starts a new burst. Runs across midnight — no calendar-day cut.
                 (30 min validated: 61% of same-lane post-booking activity falls
                 inside 30 min, thinning sharply after.)
   2. REQUIREMENT  One lane (pickup_pincode + drop_pincode) inside one burst.
                 Two lanes in one burst = two requirements. Same lane on a
                 different day = two requirements (two shipments).
   3. QUALIFYING  APP: at least ONE deviation from the app's hardcoded prefill,
                 across drop pincode / weight / dimensions.
                 WEB PORTAL: always qualifies — the requirement is stated by
                 the consignor to a KAM, not inferred, so prefill logic does
                 not apply.
   4. REPRESENTATIVE ROW  Within a requirement, the row that carries dimensions
                 and is latest; if no row carries dimensions, simply the latest.
                 GROUND TRUTH OVERRIDES THE HEURISTIC: a booked row is always
                 its own requirement, so the heuristic only picks a
                 representative for requirements with ZERO bookings. A lane-burst
                 containing N separately-booked price checks is N requirements
                 (a consignor can book two shipments on one lane inside 30 min).
                 Result: 100% of booked browsing_ids carry is_requirement = 1.

   SERVICE TYPE IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the deviation score. The app ships
   a WAREHOUSE_TO_WAREHOUSE default while 82% of bookings are DOOR_TO_DOOR, so
   nearly every consignor taps it. It carried 1,129 requirements (9.1%) on that
   single tap alone and predicts nothing.

   VALIDATION
   ----------
   Scored against 1,351 August bookings (ground truth = requested_weight on the
   booked browsing row). The representative-row rule recovers the booked weight
   in 95.1% of booked requirements overall. It beats a plain "last call" rule in
   exactly one place — APP multi-weight bursts carrying dimensions (n=459),
   80.4% -> 93.2% — and is arithmetically identical everywhere else.
   The chosen row IS the booked row for 519/578 APP and 736/781 WEB PORTAL
   booked rows.

   AUGUST 2026 BASELINE (1-26 Aug)
   -------------------------------
     APP          45,609 rate calls -> 12,343 lane-bursts -> 10,055 requirements
                  (2,331 idle lane-bursts, no requirement expressed)
     WEB PORTAL    4,964 rate calls ->  2,732 requirements (all stated)
     TOTAL        50,573 rate calls -> 12,787 requirements   ~4.0x correction

   DEMAND COMPLETENESS (checked 27 Aug 2026, 1,442 Aug demands)
   -----------------------------------------------------------
     1,384 demands carry a browsing_id; ALL of them resolve to a browsing row
     inside a flagged requirement. Nothing is lost to the deviation gate --
     no booked browsing_id ever landed in an IDLE lane-burst.
     58 demands (4.0%) carry NO browsing_id at all and are structurally
     unlinkable to any price check -- ask tech which flow bypasses the price
     check; if this share grows the metric understates demand.
     1,384 demand rows -> 1,359 distinct browsing_ids, so 25 price checks each
     produced more than one demand. REQUIREMENT -> DEMAND IS NOT 1:1.

   JOIN RULE
   ---------
   Attribute demands to requirements via requirement_key, NOT by joining on the
   flagged browsing_id. 7.7% of booked rows are edit-trail rows within their
   requirement; a join on the flagged row silently drops them.

   KNOWN LIMITATIONS
   -----------------
   a) PICKUP IS NOT SCORED. Its prefill is per-consignor (stored city), so
      touched vs untouched is undetectable without the v1_compare event payload.
      The gate is conservative by that much.
   b) DIMENSIONS FLAG IS COARSE. fact_ptl_browsing.length is only the FIRST
      material line. The real payload is the materiallist JSON array. Also uom
      mixes CM and INCH — a mix-up changes volumetric weight ~16x.
   c) NOT YET VALIDATED FOR NON-BOOKERS. 71% of APP requirements never supply
      dimensions and convert at 0.34%; the validation set contains almost no
      such cases, so weight attribution there is inference, not measurement.
   d) BLOCKED SOURCES (as of 27 Aug 2026, permission denied):
        analytics.consigner_app_events_current_v2
        analytics.consigner_app_events_current
        de_analytics.*            (event tables — engagement + prefill payload)
        trucking.dpdvib_check_price_data   (the rate actually displayed)
      Restoring (a) closes the pickup gap and validates (c); restoring the
      rate table answers "did he leave because the price was bad".
   e) DEDUPE BOOKINGS BEFORE JOINING. Some browsing_ids appear on more than one
      row of fact_ptl_bookings; a naive join inflates the browsing row count.
      The bkd CTE below handles this — do not remove it.

   ============================================================================= */


/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. ROW-LEVEL LABELLED VIEW
   Every rate call keeps its place. Nothing is deleted — the non-representative
   rows are the EDIT TRAIL and are the only record of what the consignor changed
   and in what order. Never count them as price checks; never throw them away.
   Deploy as a view, or materialise incrementally on browsing_time.

   ;


/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2. STANDING METRIC ROLLUP
   Wrap the view above as vw_ptl_requirement_labelled, then:

   SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', browsing_time)              AS wk,
          source,
          COUNT(*)                                        AS rate_calls,
          SUM(is_requirement)                             AS requirements,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_1_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_2_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_3_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND req_has_dimensions = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_with_dimensions,
          SUM(CASE WHEN requirement_type = 'IDLE_NO_REQUIREMENT'
                    AND is_representative_row = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS idle_lane_bursts,
          SUM(is_booked)                                  AS booked
   FROM   mp_analytics_core.vw_ptl_requirement_labelled
   GROUP  BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

   REPORT REQUIREMENTS SPLIT BY DEVIATION DEPTH, NOT AS A SINGLE NUMBER.
   Depth is an OUTCOME, not a quality gate — a consignor who changed only the
   drop and left is a requirement we LOST, not a weak requirement. But a single
   headline number is dominated by shallow requirements that never convert
   (drop-only: 3,882 requirements, 0 bookings), so if the widget gets more
   1-click the number rises while trips do not. The depth mix is the guardrail.

   Aug 2026 conversion by dimensions, APP requirements:
       dimensions supplied  2,907 req -> 511 booked  17.6%
       no dimensions        7,105 req ->  24 booked   0.34%       52x gap
   PTL prices on volumetric weight, so a quote computed without dimensions
   cannot be honoured — 71% of requirements are shown a price that is not real.

   METABASE NOTE
   -------------
   Do NOT leave a trailing semicolon or a trailing comment block after
   "FROM lab". Metabase wraps a native query as
   SELECT ... FROM (<your sql>) AS source when you use Explore results or add a
   filter, and a ';' inside those parentheses is a syntax error.
   To count requirements: filter is_requirement = 1, then Count of rows.
   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

-- CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW mp_analytics_core.vw_ptl_requirement_labelled AS
WITH bkd AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT CAST(browsing_id AS bigint) AS bid
    FROM   mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_bookings
    WHERE  browsing_id IS NOT NULL AND browsing_id <> ''
),
base AS (
    SELECT br.browsing_id,
           br.consigner_user_code,
           br.browsing_time,
           br.source,
           br.pickup_pincode,
           br.drop_pincode,
           br.requested_weight,
           br.service_type,
           br.materiallist,
           br.uom,
           -- dimensions present on this call (coarse: first material line only)
           CASE WHEN br.length IS NULL
                  OR br.length IN ('','0','0.0','null','NULL')
                THEN 0 ELSE 1 END                                   AS has_dim,
           -- deviation flags vs the app's hardcoded prefill constants
           CASE WHEN br.drop_pincode <> '560001'          THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS f_drop,
           CASE WHEN COALESCE(br.requested_weight,-1) <> 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS f_wt,
           CASE WHEN bkd.bid IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END              AS is_booked
    FROM   mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_browsing br
    LEFT   JOIN bkd ON bkd.bid = br.browsing_id
    WHERE  br.browsing_time >= DATE '2026-01-01'      -- <<< date window
),
brk AS (   -- 30-minute inactivity gap opens a new burst
    SELECT base.*,
           CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(minute,
                      LAG(browsing_time) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source
                                               ORDER BY browsing_time, browsing_id),
                      browsing_time) < 30
                THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS nb
    FROM   base
),
bst AS (   -- running sum turns boundary flags into a burst number
    SELECT brk.*,
           SUM(nb) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source
                         ORDER BY browsing_time, browsing_id
                         ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS burst_no
    FROM   brk
),
lab AS (
    SELECT bst.*,
           -- deviation score is STICKY across the requirement: "did he move this
           -- field off the prefill at any point in this requirement"
             MAX(f_drop)  OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
           + MAX(f_wt)    OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
           + MAX(has_dim) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS deviation_score,
           MAX(has_dim) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS req_has_dimensions,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS calls_in_requirement,
           -- how many separately-booked price checks sit in this lane-burst
           SUM(is_booked) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS booked_in_requirement,
           -- representative row: booked row wins, then dimensions, then latest
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no,
                                           pickup_pincode, drop_pincode
                              ORDER BY is_booked DESC, has_dim DESC,
                                       browsing_time DESC, browsing_id DESC)
             AS rep_rn
    FROM   bst
),

final as(SELECT browsing_id,
       a.consigner_user_code,
       browsing_time,
       source,
       pickup_pincode,
       drop_pincode,
       requested_weight,
       service_type,
       uom,
       materiallist,
       a.consigner_user_code || '|' || source || '|' || burst_no::varchar
         || '|' || pickup_pincode || '|' || drop_pincode        AS requirement_key,
       calls_in_requirement,
       booked_in_requirement,
       deviation_score,
       req_has_dimensions,
       CASE WHEN is_booked = 1            THEN 'BOOKED'
            WHEN source = 'WEB PORTAL'    THEN 'PORTAL_STATED'
            WHEN deviation_score >= 1     THEN 'APP_INFERRED'
            ELSE 'IDLE_NO_REQUIREMENT' END                      AS requirement_type,
       -- THE FLAG. Ground truth first: every booked row is its own requirement.
       -- The heuristic pick only applies where the lane-burst has no booking.
       CASE WHEN is_booked = 1 THEN 1
            WHEN booked_in_requirement = 0
             AND rep_rn = 1
             AND (source = 'WEB PORTAL' OR deviation_score >= 1) THEN 1
            ELSE 0 END                                          AS is_requirement,
       CASE WHEN rep_rn = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                   AS is_representative_row,
       is_booked
FROM   lab as a
LEFT JOIN (
Select 
consigner_user_code,
min(case when ptl_trip_rank = 1 then demand_time else null end) as first_trip_time, 
min(case when ptl_trip_rank = 3 then demand_time else null end) as third_trip_time
from mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_bookings
where demand_status = 'FULFILLED'
group by 1
) as b on b.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT user_code,
  max(case when flow_type_config_id = 17 then 1 else 0 end) as test1,
  max(case when flow_type_config_id = 18 then 1 else 0 end) as control1,
  max(case when flow_type_config_id = 36 then 1 else 0 end) as control2,
  max(case when flow_type_config_id = 37 then 1 else 0 end) as test2
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_experiment_user_allocation
where flow_type_config_id in (17,18,36,37)
GROUP BY 1
) as c on c.user_code = a.consigner_user_code
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT consigner_user_code, max(consigner_region) as consigner_region
FROM mp_analytics_core.fact_lead_state
GROUP BY 1
) as r on r.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code
where 
  browsing_time::date >= case 
    when {{Interval}} = 'Day' then current_date - interval '14 days'
    when {{Interval}} = 'Week' then current_date - interval '14 weeks'
    when {{Interval}} = 'Month' then current_date - interval '12 months'
    else current_date - interval '14 days' 
  end
[[and (case 
	when browsing_time<=first_trip_time 
	or first_trip_time is null then 'New'
	when browsing_time<=third_trip_time  then '1-3'
	when browsing_time>third_trip_time then '3+' else null end)
in ({{cx_segment_ptl}})
]]
[[and (
 (case when c.test1 = 1 then 'Test1' else 'NA' end) in ({{exp_type}})
 or (case when c.control1 = 1 then 'Control1' else 'NA' end) in ({{exp_type}})
 or (case when c.control2 = 1 then 'Control2' else 'NA' end) in ({{exp_type}})
 or (case when c.test2 = 1 then 'Test2' else 'NA' end) in ({{exp_type}})
 or (case when coalesce(c.test1,0)+coalesce(c.control1,0)+coalesce(c.control2,0)+coalesce(c.test2,0) = 0 then 'Other' else 'NA' end) in ({{exp_type}})
)]]
[[and r.consigner_region in ({{consigner_region}})
]]

)

select 
date_trunc({{Interval}}, browsing_time) as interval,
sum(is_requirement) as "# Price Search"

from final

group by 1
Order by 1 desc

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: # Price Search Customers; Price-Checking Cx.

Distinct consigners who did at least one PTL price search in the interval. Customer-level counterpart of # Price Search (which is requirement-level).

Note: this card counts distinct consigner_user_code on RAW fact_ptl_browsing rows — it does NOT apply the requirement/burst de-dup logic. De-dup is irrelevant at Cx grain (a customer is counted once regardless of how many re-quotes fired).

Cx segment here is derived from browsing_time vs the consigner's 1st and 3rd FULFILLED PTL trip time: New (before 1st trip or never tripped), 1-3, 3+.
Filters: Interval, cx_segment_ptl, exp_type, consigner_region.
SQL:
Select 
  date_trunc({{Interval}}, browsing_time) as interval,
  count(distinct a.consigner_user_code) as "# Price Search Cx"
from mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_browsing as a
LEFT JOIN (
Select 
consigner_user_code,
min(case when ptl_trip_rank = 1 then demand_time else null end) as first_trip_time, 
min(case when ptl_trip_rank = 3 then demand_time else null end) as third_trip_time
from mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_bookings
where demand_status = 'FULFILLED'

group by 1
) as b on b.consigner_user_code = a.consigner_user_code
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT user_code,
  max(case when flow_type_config_id = 17 then 1 else 0 end) as test1,

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Requirement -> Booking %; Search-to-Book Conversion.

% of PTL requirements that converted into a booking. Numerator = requirements with a linked demand; denominator = all qualifying requirements (is_requirement = 1).

Uses the SAME requirement definition as # Price Search (30-min burst + lane + prefill-deviation gate, representative row, booked rows always their own requirement) — see # Price Search for the full locked definition.

Join rule: demands are attributed back to the browsing row / requirement that produced them. Caveat: 4.0% of demands carry no browsing_id and cannot be linked, and 25 of 1,384 Aug demands came from a single price check, so Requirement -> Demand is not strictly 1:1.

Definition locked 27 Aug 2026. Owner: PTL Demand POD.
Filters: Interval, cx_segment_ptl, exp_type, consigner_region.
SQL:
/* =============================================================================
   PTL CONSIGNOR REQUIREMENT — STANDING METRIC
   =============================================================================
   Owner        : PTL Demand POD
   Purpose      : Replace "price checks" (raw rows in fact_ptl_browsing) with
                  "requirements" — one row per distinct shipment intent.
   Last updated : 27 Aug 2026

   WHY THIS EXISTS
   
   ---------------
   fact_ptl_browsing is at RATE-API-CALL grain, not user-action grain. A new
   browsing_id is minted on every rate call, including the silent re-quotes
   fired when a consignor edits anything while sitting on the transporter
   listing page. Counting rows overstates consignor demand ~4x.

   DEFINITION (locked 27 Aug 2026)
   -------------------------------
   1. BURST      A consignor's chain of rate calls; a gap of >= 30 minutes
                 starts a new burst. Runs across midnight — no calendar-day cut.
                 (30 min validated: 61% of same-lane post-booking activity falls
                 inside 30 min, thinning sharply after.)
   2. REQUIREMENT  One lane (pickup_pincode + drop_pincode) inside one burst.
                 Two lanes in one burst = two requirements. Same lane on a
                 different day = two requirements (two shipments).
   3. QUALIFYING  APP: at least ONE deviation from the app's hardcoded prefill,
                 across drop pincode / weight / dimensions.
                 WEB PORTAL: always qualifies — the requirement is stated by
                 the consignor to a KAM, not inferred, so prefill logic does
                 not apply.
   4. REPRESENTATIVE ROW  Within a requirement, the row that carries dimensions
                 and is latest; if no row carries dimensions, simply the latest.
                 GROUND TRUTH OVERRIDES THE HEURISTIC: a booked row is always
                 its own requirement, so the heuristic only picks a
                 representative for requirements with ZERO bookings. A lane-burst
                 containing N separately-booked price checks is N requirements
                 (a consignor can book two shipments on one lane inside 30 min).
                 Result: 100% of booked browsing_ids carry is_requirement = 1.

   SERVICE TYPE IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the deviation score. The app ships
   a WAREHOUSE_TO_WAREHOUSE default while 82% of bookings are DOOR_TO_DOOR, so
   nearly every consignor taps it. It carried 1,129 requirements (9.1%) on that
   single tap alone and predicts nothing.

   VALIDATION
   ----------
   Scored against 1,351 August bookings (ground truth = requested_weight on the
   booked browsing row). The representative-row rule recovers the booked weight
   in 95.1% of booked requirements overall. It beats a plain "last call" rule in
   exactly one place — APP multi-weight bursts carrying dimensions (n=459),
   80.4% -> 93.2% — and is arithmetically identical everywhere else.
   The chosen row IS the booked row for 519/578 APP and 736/781 WEB PORTAL
   booked rows.

   AUGUST 2026 BASELINE (1-26 Aug)
   -------------------------------
     APP          45,609 rate calls -> 12,343 lane-bursts -> 10,055 requirements
                  (2,331 idle lane-bursts, no requirement expressed)
     WEB PORTAL    4,964 rate calls ->  2,732 requirements (all stated)
     TOTAL        50,573 rate calls -> 12,787 requirements   ~4.0x correction

   DEMAND COMPLETENESS (checked 27 Aug 2026, 1,442 Aug demands)
   -----------------------------------------------------------
     1,384 demands carry a browsing_id; ALL of them resolve to a browsing row
     inside a flagged requirement. Nothing is lost to the deviation gate --
     no booked browsing_id ever landed in an IDLE lane-burst.
     58 demands (4.0%) carry NO browsing_id at all and are structurally
     unlinkable to any price check -- ask tech which flow bypasses the price
     check; if this share grows the metric understates demand.
     1,384 demand rows -> 1,359 distinct browsing_ids, so 25 price checks each
     produced more than one demand. REQUIREMENT -> DEMAND IS NOT 1:1.

   JOIN RULE
   ---------
   Attribute demands to requirements via requirement_key, NOT by joining on the
   flagged browsing_id. 7.7% of booked rows are edit-trail rows within their
   requirement; a join on the flagged row silently drops them.

   KNOWN LIMITATIONS
   -----------------
   a) PICKUP IS NOT SCORED. Its prefill is per-consignor (stored city), so
      touched vs untouched is undetectable without the v1_compare event payload.
      The gate is conservative by that much.
   b) DIMENSIONS FLAG IS COARSE. fact_ptl_browsing.length is only the FIRST
      material line. The real payload is the materiallist JSON array. Also uom
      mixes CM and INCH — a mix-up changes volumetric weight ~16x.
   c) NOT YET VALIDATED FOR NON-BOOKERS. 71% of APP requirements never supply
      dimensions and convert at 0.34%; the validation set contains almost no
      such cases, so weight attribution there is inference, not measurement.
   d) BLOCKED SOURCES (as of 27 Aug 2026, permission denied):
        analytics.consigner_app_events_current_v2
        analytics.consigner_app_events_current
        de_analytics.*            (event tables — engagement + prefill payload)
        trucking.dpdvib_check_price_data   (the rate actually displayed)
      Restoring (a) closes the pickup gap and validates (c); restoring the
      rate table answers "did he leave because the price was bad".
   e) DEDUPE BOOKINGS BEFORE JOINING. Some browsing_ids appear on more than one
      row of fact_ptl_bookings; a naive join inflates the browsing row count.
      The bkd CTE below handles this — do not remove it.

   ============================================================================= */


/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. ROW-LEVEL LABELLED VIEW
   Every rate call keeps its place. Nothing is deleted — the non-representative
   rows are the EDIT TRAIL and are the only record of what the consignor changed
   and in what order. Never count them as price checks; never throw them away.
   Deploy as a view, or materialise incrementally on browsing_time.

   ;


/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2. STANDING METRIC ROLLUP
   Wrap the view above as vw_ptl_requirement_labelled, then:

   SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', browsing_time)              AS wk,
          source,
          COUNT(*)                                        AS rate_calls,
          SUM(is_requirement)                             AS requirements,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_1_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_2_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND deviation_score = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_3_change,
          SUM(CASE WHEN is_requirement = 1 AND req_has_dimensions = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS req_with_dimensions,
          SUM(CASE WHEN requirement_type = 'IDLE_NO_REQUIREMENT'
                    AND is_representative_row = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS idle_lane_bursts,
          SUM(is_booked)                                  AS booked
   FROM   mp_analytics_core.vw_ptl_requirement_labelled
   GROUP  BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

   REPORT REQUIREMENTS SPLIT BY DEVIATION DEPTH, NOT AS A SINGLE NUMBER.
   Depth is an OUTCOME, not a quality gate — a consignor who changed only the
   drop and left is a requirement we LOST, not a weak requirement. But a single
   headline number is dominated by shallow requirements that never convert
   (drop-only: 3,882 requirements, 0 bookings), so if the widget gets more
   1-click the number rises while trips do not. The depth mix is the guardrail.

   Aug 2026 conversion by dimensions, APP requirements:
       dimensions supplied  2,907 req -> 511 booked  17.6%
       no dimensions        7,105 req ->  24 booked   0.34%       52x gap
   PTL prices on volumetric weight, so a quote computed without dimensions
   cannot be honoured — 71% of requirements are shown a price that is not real.

   METABASE NOTE
   -------------
   Do NOT leave a trailing semicolon or a trailing comment block after
   "FROM lab". Metabase wraps a native query as
   SELECT ... FROM (<your sql>) AS source when you use Explore results or add a
   filter, and a ';' inside those parentheses is a syntax error.
   To count requirements: filter is_requirement = 1, then Count of rows.
   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

-- CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW mp_analytics_core.vw_ptl_requirement_labelled AS
WITH bkd AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT CAST(browsing_id AS bigint) AS bid
    FROM   mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_bookings
    WHERE  browsing_id IS NOT NULL AND browsing_id <> ''
	and placement_flag = 1
),
base AS (
    SELECT br.browsing_id,
           br.consigner_user_code,
           br.browsing_time,
           br.source,
           br.pickup_pincode,
           br.drop_pincode,
           br.requested_weight,
           br.service_type,
           br.materiallist,
           br.uom,
           -- dimensions present on this call (coarse: first material line only)
           CASE WHEN br.length IS NULL
                  OR br.length IN ('','0','0.0','null','NULL')
                THEN 0 ELSE 1 END                                   AS has_dim,
           -- deviation flags vs the app's hardcoded prefill constants
           CASE WHEN br.drop_pincode <> '560001'          THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS f_drop,
           CASE WHEN COALESCE(br.requested_weight,-1) <> 200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS f_wt,
           CASE WHEN bkd.bid IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END              AS is_booked
    FROM   mp_analytics_core.fact_ptl_browsing br
    LEFT   JOIN bkd ON bkd.bid = br.browsing_id
    WHERE  br.browsing_time >= DATE '2026-01-01'      -- <<< date window
),
brk AS (   -- 30-minute inactivity gap opens a new burst
    SELECT base.*,
           CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(minute,
                      LAG(browsing_time) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source
                                               ORDER BY browsing_time, browsing_id),
                      browsing_time) < 30
                THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS nb
    FROM   base
),
bst AS (   -- running sum turns boundary flags into a burst number
    SELECT brk.*,
           SUM(nb) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source
                         ORDER BY browsing_time, browsing_id
                         ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS burst_no
    FROM   brk
),
lab AS (
    SELECT bst.*,
           -- deviation score is STICKY across the requirement: "did he move this
           -- field off the prefill at any point in this requirement"
             MAX(f_drop)  OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
           + MAX(f_wt)    OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
           + MAX(has_dim) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS deviation_score,
           MAX(has_dim) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS req_has_dimensions,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS calls_in_requirement,
           -- how many separately-booked price checks sit in this lane-burst
           SUM(is_booked) OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no, pickup_pincode, drop_pincode)
             AS booked_in_requirement,
           -- representative row: booked row wins, then dimensions, then latest
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY consigner_user_code, source, burst_no,
                                           pickup_pincode, drop_pincode

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: PTL Recovery Curve; Collection Efficiency (D+7/15/30).

Six payment-health ratios on PTL receivables, all as % of receivable_before_settlement, from mp_analytics_core.as_trip_payments, bucketed on demand_time:
- Recovery within due date
- Recovery within D+7  (denominator restricted to days_since_due >= 7)
- Recovery within D+15 (days_since_due >= 15)
- Recovery within D+30 (days_since_due >= 30)
- Gross NPA (days_since_due >= 90)
- Net NPA  (days_since_due >= 180)

Each bucket restricts BOTH numerator and denominator to receivables that have actually aged past that threshold — so D+30 is not diluted by invoices only 5 days old.
Recovered amounts are stored negative and multiplied by -1 to present as positive %.

date_trunc({{Interval}},a.demand_time)::Date as month,
sum(-1*recovered_within_due_date)*100/nullif(sum(receivable_before_settlement),0) as recovery_with_due_date,

/nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=7 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as recovery_with_due_date7,

/nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=15 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as recovery_with_due_date15,

/nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=90 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as gross_npa,

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Tutorial Cohort Funnel; v1_ptl_tutorial_view Impact.

Full PTL funnel (active -> landed -> price check -> demand -> placement -> trip) reported three ways: overall, for the tutorial cohort (users who fired the v1_ptl_tutorial_view event), and as the tutorial cohort's contribution to each overall step.

Per step it outputs: absolute users, % of active users, tutorial-cohort % (tut_*_pct, denominated on tutorial users), and the tutorial share of the overall step.

Used to answer "is the PTL tutorial actually pulling users down the funnel, or is it just being seen by users who would have converted anyway?" Read as directional — it is an observational cohort comparison, not a randomised experiment, so tutorial viewers are self-selected.
SQL:
select
  interval,
  count(distinct user_code) as active_users,
  sum(landed) as landed_users,
  sum(landed)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as landed_pct,
  sum(price_check) as price_check_users,
  sum(price_check)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as price_check_pct,
  sum(demand) as demand_users,
  sum(demand)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as demand_pct,
  sum(placement) as placement_users,
  
  sum(placement)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as placement_pct,
  sum(trip) as trip_users,
  sum(trip)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as trip_pct,

  -- tutorial cohort
  count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end) as tut_users,
  count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as tut_reach_pct,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then landed else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end),0) as tut_landed_pct,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then price_check else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end),0) as tut_price_check_pct,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then demand else 0 end) as tut_demand_users,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then demand else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end),0) as tut_demand_pct,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then placement else 0 end) as tut_placement_users,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then placement else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end),0) as tut_placement_pct,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then trip else 0 end) as tut_trip_users,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then trip else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct case when tutorial=1 then user_code end),0) as tut_trip_pct,

  -- contribution of tutorial cohort to overall (pp)
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then landed else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as landed_contrib_tut_pp,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then price_check else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as price_check_contrib_tut_pp,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then demand else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as demand_contrib_tut_pp,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then placement else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as placement_contrib_tut_pp,
  sum(case when tutorial=1 then trip else 0 end)*100.0/nullif(count(distinct user_code),0) as trip_contrib_tut_pp
from (
Select 
date_trunc({{Interval}},event_date) as interval,
a.user_code,
max(case when screen_name ilike '%ptl_home_page%' then 1 else 0 end) as landed,

Meaning / Logic:
Aliases: Onboarding Cohort Recovery; New-Cx Collection Curve.
 
 The full recovery / NPA panel (within due date, D+7, D+15, D+30, Gross NPA, Net NPA — all as % of receivable_before_settlement) restricted to ACQUISITION customers: trip_rank <= 3.
 
 Same bucket-aware construction as % Recovery (D+7/15/30) — each ratio restricts numerator and denominator to receivables aged past that threshold (>=7, >=15, >=30, >=90, >=180 days_since_due).
 
 Monthly grain on due_date, trailing 12 months, ptl_flag = 1. Recovered amounts stored negative, sign-flipped for display.
 Paired with % Recovery Retention Cx to show whether credit risk sits with new or repeat customers.
SQL:
Select 
 date_trunc('month',due_date)::Date as month,
 sum(-1*recovered_within_due_date)*100/nullif(sum(receivable_before_settlement),0) as recovery_with_due_date,
 sum(case when days_since_due>=7 then -1*recovered_within_7_days else null end)*100
 /nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=7 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as recovery_with_due_date7,
 sum(case when days_since_due>=15 then -1*recovered_within_15_days else null end)*100
 /nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=15 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as recovery_with_due_date15,
 sum(case when days_since_due>=30 then -1*recovered_within_30_days else null end)*100
 /nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=30 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as recovery_with_due_date30,
 
 sum(case when days_since_due>=90 then demand_gross_npa else null end)*100
 /nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=90 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as gross_npa,
 
 sum(case when days_since_due>=180 then demand_net_npa else null end)*100
 /nullif(sum(case when days_since_due>=180 then receivable_before_settlement else null end),0) as net_npa
 
 from mp_analytics_core.as_trip_payments
 where ptl_flag = 1
 and due_date::date<=current_date
 and date_trunc('month',due_date) >= date_trunc('month',current_date)-interval '12 month'
 and trip_rank<=3
 group by 1
 order by 1 desc
